newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault warns of bigger losses.
newsitem.headline: Renault warns of bigger losses.

text.p: French carmaker Renault sounded a fresh warning Friday about its 1996 results, saying its operating loss would be much worse than market expectations.
Shares in the company, which said previously it expected to lose money on both its car and truck operations and report its first annual loss in 10 years, fell on the news.

French car sales fell 34 percent in January, revealing the market's underlying weakness after more than two years of state support through incentives for people to buy new vehicles. The incentives ended last fall.
"France is a pretty nasty place to try to sell cars," one industry analyst said.

Analysts had pencilled in an operating loss of between 1.3 billion francs ($229 million) and 1.6 billion francs ($281 million) for Renault, whose profit margins were eroded last year by a savage price war among carmakers fighting to boost their share of Europe's slow-growing market.

"In view of the prevailing economic context, and despite the increase in revenues of the automobile division ... the operating loss to be reported by Renault Group for 1996 will be considerably higher than that generally anticipated by the financial markets," Renault said in a statement.
It said its performance last year was marred by "relentless and aggressive price wars," which drove up marketing costs, and lower truck sales in the United States, where Renault owns Mack Trucks.

Renault said its 1996 sales totalled 184.08 billion francs ($32.4 billion), virtually unchanged from the previous year's 184.07 billion, as a 9.5 percent drop in truck sales offset a 2.3 percent gain in the car division.
